caveats: doc 47 SS18.5 (binding): a bound is stated together with the population it bounds. Rows whose bound_provenance.population is 'band centres' bound the BAND GEOMETRY, not the finite noun inventory the circuit was actually trained on. A measurement above such a bound is not necessarily an error.

exp61's CONFIRM stage (doc 47 SS18, fresh draw sha 99fdafb3) measured M2w/S1 = 0.8880 against the 0.8750 corrected BAND ceiling -- above it by +0.0130 -- and doc 47 SS18.1 attributes that to the population mismatch, not to a broken bound. Those confirm numbers live in doc 47 SS18 and in no committed results_*.json, so they are NOT rows in this table.

exp62's bounds are CONSTRUCTIVE LOWER bounds from a budgeted search over the actual held-out noun angles of their own draw. Ratios above 1.0 there mean the search did not find the optimum, not that the circuit beat capacity.

exp65's and exp67's bounds are DOC-REGISTERED: computed in sessions whose code was never committed. They are carried with that provenance and are not re-derived by this script. exp67's is empirically corroborated by its classical comparator landing on it (doc 53 comparator meta_notes).
exp65's bound of 1.0000 cannot test a cap: doc 51 SS11.3 records that 15.8% of random 3-vs-5 splits of its 8 held-out words also reach 1.0000.

doc 54 SS7 read NO exp68 criterion against a bound, and doc 52 SS2.2 removed a 9-dim-per-referent bound's standing as an instrument on a 24-noun inventory. exp68's rows are validation of the INSTRUMENT, not a re-reading of exp68's verdicts.

Every arm here is a simulation of a product-state encoding whose kernel doc 52 SS1 proved factorises and is classically O(n). Nothing in this table is a quantum-advantage claim, and the classical-comparator rows are in the figure precisely so that it cannot be read as one.
